investigations.name: biogears-hemorrhage
investigations.title: Hemorrhage and resuscitation in the BioGears engine
investigations.description: Three studies on the biogears_hemorrhage and biogears_resuscitation composites, run through the workbench and recorded in each study's runs.db. Their pass criteria are pytest files in each study's tests/ directory, written after a 2026-11-16 pilot of every arm (the same composites and parameters, run directly) and fixed before the canonical runs.
investigations.question: How does the BioGears 8.2.0 engine respond to a hemorrhage: how does the response scale with the bleed rate, does closed-loop fluid resuscitation change it, and does the same bleed behave the same across BioGears' 17 shipped patients? (viva-pulse's pulse-hemorrhage investigation, ported to BioGears.)
investigations.hypothesis: Blood loss, the heart-rate rise and the MAP fall all grow with the bleed rate, less than in proportion because BioGears lowers a bleed with the local pressure; a MAP-targeted infusion preserves blood volume and pressure; every shipped patient compensates, smaller patients and those with a higher resting cardiac output losing more.

investigations.name: biogears-timestep
investigations.title: BioGears' solver time step - accuracy and speed
investigations.description: Both studies run the same composite at time_step_s 0.02, 0.04 and 0.08 (the new time_step_s parameter of every viva-biogears process, passed to BioGears through pybiogears' configuration override) and compare each run with the 0.02 s run. Their criteria were written after a pilot of every arm (workspace/experiments/timestep-pilot-2026-11-16).
investigations.question: How much accuracy and speed do BioGears' solver steps of 0.04 and 0.08 s trade against its validated 0.02 s, in a fast process (a 5 min hemorrhage) and a slow one (the first 6 h of a severe infection)?
investigations.hypothesis: Volumes, hemodynamics and the inflammatory response stay close to the 0.02 s runs, and the larger steps run two to three times faster; but lactate breaks above 0.02 s, and at 0.08 s BioGears crashes about 6.5 min into a 200 mL/min bleed, so 0.02 s remains the step to use for anything but quick, short exploration.

investigations.name: mcdaniel-2019
investigations.title: Replicating McDaniel et al. 2019 (sepsis in BioGears) on BioGears 8.2.0
investigations.description: Three studies on the biogears_sepsis composite. Its treatment parameter runs the paper's protocols (viva_biogears.protocols, TreatmentController). The progression arms run 48 h from t = 0; as in the paper, every treatment arm starts from the severe infection's state saved at 44 h (viva_biogears/states/StandardMale@severe-infection-44h.xml) and runs 8-20 h. mcdaniel-2019-sepsis/run.py runs the same arms outside the workbench, and analyze.py draws the paper's figures. Fig 8 (inflammation parameter changes) needs changes inside BioGears and is out of scope.
investigations.question: Does BioGears 8.2.0, driven through viva-biogears, reproduce McDaniel et al. (2019): sepsis progression by infection severity (Figs 4-7), the fluid challenge and antibiotic (Figs 9-10), and the REFRESH resuscitation protocols, on time and delayed (Figs 11-13)?
investigations.hypothesis: The progression follows the paper up to hypotension, but on 8.2.0 the severe arm does not reach septic shock by 48 h; the treatments act as the paper describes: the challenge restores volume, piperacillin exceeds the MIC and lowers the pathogen, both REFRESH protocols reach the goals with the experimental one using less fluid, and a 12 h delay costs more fluid.
